exercise.name: Side Bridge with Bent Leg

reference.title: Side Bridge with Bent Leg (male)
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Isometric-dynamic (lateral trunk and hip lift on the forearm and knee)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you lift the hips, breathe steadily in the hold, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, 3 s hold, 1.5 s down

prescription.reps: 6-10 lifts with a 3 s hold (or 10-30 s holds)
prescription.progression: Longer holds, then the full side plank on the feet

cues.text: Lie on your right side, propped on the right forearm with the elbow under the shoulder; knees bent about 90 degrees, legs stacked, hips on the mat.
Breathe out, press the forearm and the outside of the knee into the mat and lift the hips.
Shoulder, hip and knee in one straight line; hips stacked, chest facing forward.
Breathe in and lower the hips to the mat with control.
Settle, then lift again; switch sides after the set.

mistakes.fix: Lift until shoulder, hip and knee line up.
Push the hips forward so the thighs stay in line with the trunk.
Push the forearm into the floor and keep the shoulder away from the ear.

mistakes.mistake: Rolling the chest toward the floor
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips and shoulders stacked.

kinematics.norm: Shoulder, hip and knee in one straight line at the top (McGill 1998)
Elbow on the mat directly under the shoulder, forearm pointing forward (clinical opinion)
Knees bent about 90 degrees; the lower knee is the pivot, which shortens the lever compared with the full side bridge (clinical opinion)
Pelvis lifts clear of the mat (clinical opinion)
Controlled lifts with a short hold, or timed holds (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #11777, Side Bridge with Bent Leg (male) (movement reference only)

Electromyographic analysis of core trunk, hip and thigh muscles during 9 rehabilitation exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 2007; PubMed 18560185)

cautions: Shoulder pain on the support side: keep the elbow right under the shoulder, or stop.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Hard on the knee: put a folded towel under it.
Too hard: hold a smaller lift.
regressions: Hip lifts of a few centimetres.
progressions: Full side plank on the feet.
Side plank with the top leg lifted.

muscleNotes.obliques_r: Main target on the down side: holds the trunk up against gravity; side bridging gives high oblique and quadratus lumborum activity with low spine load (McGill 1998).
muscleNotes.core: Quadratus lumborum and the deep abdominals hold the trunk straight (McGill, Juker and Kropf).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Lifts and holds the pelvis from below (hip abduction on the down side; Ekstrom 2007 found high gluteus medius activity in the side bridge).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the supporting shoulder blade on the ribs.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Supports the shoulder over the elbow.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: The top leg presses down on the bottom leg.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Keeps the hips extended in line with the trunk.
